nodes.title: FET Phase
nodes.description: Further Education and Training Phase (Grades 10-12)

nodes.title: Grade 12
History
nodes.description: History — Grade 12 — CAPS Curriculum

nodes.title: Term 1
nodes.description: Extension of the Cold War, Independent Africa, Civil Society Protests 1950s–1990s

nodes.title: Topic 1: Extension of the Cold War
nodes.description: The origins of the Cold War in Europe and the Cold War case study of Vietnam.

nodes.title: Origins of the Cold War in Europe
nodes.description: End of the Second World War (introduction) and why a Cold War developed; USSR and USA creation of spheres of interest (installation of Soviet-friendly governments in satellite states); USA's policy of containment: Truman Doctrine, Marshall Plan, the Berlin Crisis 1949–1961, NATO and the Warsaw Pact; who was to blame for the Cold War? [Source-based focus]

nodes.title: Cold War Case Study: Vietnam
nodes.description: 1957–1965: struggle in Vietnam between the South Vietnamese army and communist-trained rebels (Viet Cong); 1965–1969: North Vietnamese–USA struggle including the nature of the Vietnamese war against the USA; the war from Vietnamese and USA perspectives; the war as a global issue; 1969–1975: USA withdrawal from Vietnam and impact on USA politics including student movements. [Essay focus]

nodes.title: Topic 2: Independent Africa
nodes.description: Africa in the Cold War with a case study on Angola, and how independence was realised in Africa in the 1960s and 1970s with a case study on the Congo.

nodes.title: Africa in the Cold War: Case Study – Angola
nodes.description: Angola: colonialism and independence; outbreak of civil war in 1974 (MPLA, FNLA and UNITA); reasons for and nature of involvement in Angola (USSR, USA, Cuba, China, South Africa) and impact on regional stability; significance of the Battle of Cuito Cuanavale 1987 and 1988; changing nature of international relationships. [Source-based focus]

nodes.title: How Independence was Realised in Africa: Case Study – The Congo
nodes.description: What were the ideas that influenced the Congo? Political factors: type of leader, legacies of colonialism, type of government, political stability and instability; economic factors: type of economy; social and cultural successes and challenges (benefits of independence, education, Africanisation). [Essay focus]

nodes.title: Topic 3: Civil Society Protests 1950s–1990s
nodes.description: The US Civil Rights Movement and the Black Power Movement.

nodes.title: The US Civil Rights Movement
nodes.description: Reasons and origins of the Civil Rights Movement in the USA; role, impact and influence of Martin Luther King Jr; forms of protest through civil disobedience: Montgomery bus boycott, sit-ins, marches including to Lincoln Memorial, Birmingham campaign and Selma-Montgomery marches; school desegregation case study: Little Rock, Arkansas; short-term and long-term gains. [Source-based focus]

nodes.title: The Black Power Movement
nodes.description: Reasons for the movement; formation of the Black Panther Party; roles of Malcolm X, Stokely Carmichael, Huey Newton and other African American activists; short-term and long-term gains. [Essay focus]

nodes.title: Term 2
nodes.description: Civil Resistance in South Africa 1970s–1980s, Coming of Democracy to South Africa, End of the Cold War, June examinations

nodes.title: Topic 4: Civil Resistance in South Africa – 1970s to 1980s
nodes.description: The challenge of Black Consciousness to the Apartheid state and the crisis of Apartheid through internal resistance.

nodes.title: The Challenge of Black Consciousness to the Apartheid State
nodes.description: The nature and aims of Black Consciousness; the role of Steve Biko; the Black Consciousness Movement (BCM); the challenge posed by the ideas of Black Consciousness to the state; the 1976 Soweto uprising (briefly, relating to BCM influence on students); the legacy of Black Consciousness on South African politics. [Essay focus]

nodes.title: The Crisis of Apartheid: Internal Resistance
nodes.description: Government attempts to reform apartheid; the 1982 Urban Bantu Authorities Act; the Tricameral system; internal resistance to reforms; growing power of the trade union movement from 1973; response to Botha's 'reforms': new methods of mobilisation including labour's rolling mass action, roles of civics, UDF, Mass Democratic Movement, End Conscription Campaign and Black Sash. [Source-based focus]

nodes.title: Topic 5: The Coming of Democracy to South Africa and Coming to Terms with the Past
nodes.description: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission and the negotiated settlement leading to the Government of National Unity.

nodes.title: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC)
nodes.description: Reasons for the TRC hearings; focus on various case studies of victims and perpetrators; the debates concerning the TRC; positive aspects of the TRC; amnesty – focus on human rights of the 1980s; reparations; responses of political parties to the TRC and the final report; focus on various case studies of victims and perpetrators. [Source-based focus]

nodes.title: Negotiated Settlement and the Government of National Unity
nodes.description: Beginning of negotiations 1990–1991; breakdown of negotiations; multi-party negotiation process resumes; ongoing violence; final road to democracy 1994 (27 April 1994 election, the Government of National Unity). [Essay focus]

nodes.title: Topic 6: The End of the Cold War and New World Order
nodes.description: The end of the Cold War, the events of 1989 and the new world order.

nodes.title: The End of the Cold War and the Events of 1989
nodes.description: Gorbachev's reforms in the Soviet Union (glasnost, perestroika); Eastern Europe in broad outline: events in Poland, significance of these events on Soviet influence in Eastern Europe, Germany and the fall of the Berlin Wall; the disintegration of the Soviet Union; turning point in South Africa: the collapse of the Soviet Union and its impact on South Africa. [Essay focus]

nodes.title: Term 3
nodes.description: A New Global World Order (Globalisation), revision of all Paper 1 and Paper 2 topics, preparatory examination

nodes.title: Topic 6 (continued): A New Global World Order – Globalisation
nodes.description: Defining globalisation; balance of power and impact on Africa; dominance of global capitalism; emerging economies and different forms of capitalism (BRICS); responses to globalisation. [Source-based focus]

nodes.title: Globalisation and the New World Order
nodes.description: Defining globalisation; balance of power and impact on Africa; dominance of global capitalism; emerging economies and different forms of capitalism including BRICS; responses to globalisation.
